newsitem.title: GERMANY: DG Bank sees 96 oper profit up over 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: DG Bank sees 96 oper profit up over 10 pct.

text.p: Deutsche Genossenschaftsbank said on Wednesday it expected operating profit before risk provisions to rise to more than 600 million marks in 1996, showing double-digit percentage growth.
In 1995 the bank swung back to profit, posting an operating profit of 554.7 million marks.
Risk provisions were likely to remain unchanged at 200 million marks for 1996, DG Bank said in a statement released ahead of its news conference in Hohenkammer near Munich.

DG Bank, which acts as central bank to Germany's co-operative banking sector, has emerged from a lengthy restructuring process after write-offs on a large and controversial bond deal with French banks caused a sharp drop in profits in 1991.
The bank said it had a balance sheet total of 175.5 billion marks at the end of September, up 8.4 percent from 161.9 billion marks at the end of 1995.
Business volume increased by 8.3 percent to 183.3 billion marks from 169.2 billion.
